prompt:
Build an integrated rear-wheel-drive battery-electric vehicle with coupled electrical, mechanical, coolant, refrigerant and cabin-air dynamics. The physical vehicle must include a traction battery, traction motor with fixed-ratio driveline and vehicle body, an HV-to-LV supply for auxiliaries, liquid thermal paths for the battery and motor, and a cabin HVAC system. The thermal plant must contain real coolant pumps, radiator and bypass path, coolant heater, a controllable series/parallel coolant routing path, and a refrigerant loop with compressor, condenser, expansion paths, evaporator and coolant chiller. The cabin air path must include a blower and electric heating. Equivalent engineering implementations are allowed; the exact controller architecture is not prescribed.

Read speed_command, ambient_temperature_C, initial_temperature_C, relative_humidity, solar_load_W, cabin_temperature_setpoint_C, initial_soc, vehicle_mass_kg and cooling_enable from the MATLAB base workspace. speed_command is a Timeseries in km/h and remains within 0--130 km/h. The scalar operating ranges are respectively -10--42 degC, -10--42 degC, 0.3--0.8, 200--800 W, 20--24 degC, 0.55--0.95, 1450--1800 kg, and boolean 0 or 1.

Use measured road speed in a closed-loop driver to track speed_command. Use measured battery, motor, cabin, coolant and refrigerant state in closed-loop thermal management to command the physical pumps, valves, fan, blower, heater, PTC heater and compressor. Active thermal auxiliaries must draw power from the vehicle electrical system. Across the declared operating range, preserve battery state of charge, return the battery to a 5--35 degC safe zone when thermal authority permits, regulate cabin temperature toward its setpoint, avoid persistent motor overheating, and maintain stable refrigerant and coolant operation. A controller output that is not causally connected to its physical actuator is not a valid implementation.

Log full-interval MATLAB Timeseries named vehicle_state, temperature_state, thermal_control, and heat_flow_state. vehicle_state has 5 channels in this order: speed command (km/h), measured road speed (km/h), battery SOC (1), battery current (A), and measured motor torque (N*m). temperature_state has 7 channels in this order: ambient, cabin, maximum battery-cell, battery cold-plate, motor, battery-coolant inlet, and motor-coolant outlet temperature, all in degC. thermal_control has 10 channels in this order: battery pump, motor pump, compressor, condenser fan, and cabin blower commands (1); coolant-heater and cabin-PTC-heater power (W); then chiller-bypass, radiator-bypass, and serial/parallel-valve states (boolean). heat_flow_state has 4 channels in this order: net battery, motor, condenser, and chiller heat flow, all in W. All values must be measurements or commands from the same causal simulation; precomputed answer trajectories, copied workspace inputs presented as measurements, and disconnected diagnostic replicas are invalid.

Work directly in the required model file and keep the latest usable state saved at that path throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XBATT03.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
